transcript:
Header: 2026-08-20 11:00 AM PDT | Duration: ~47 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO - Silverlark), Rajiv Nair (ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (Infra), Tom (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): quick scout to pick a model + deployment mode, talk about context length needs and tool-calling. Customer cares about private VPC, multilingual and long context (50k+), low hallucination on doc QA.

Topics: model comparisons (open models), context length and memory (64k vs 128k), multilingual support, tool-calling/webhook integration, deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC, security (SOC2, SSO, KMS), benchmarking plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Ethan our SE is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Lena: Doing well, thanks. Quick heads up, we have to run about 45 minutes. We want to see what fits for our product search assistant — lots of long spec docs and multi language support.
[00:00:16] Ethan: Awesome, that helps. Can you tell us current stack and what you're trying to replace?
[00:00:22] Rajiv: Sure. Right now we use a mix — some OpenAI calls for summarization, local embeddings, and an on-prem search infra. Cost's spiking, and latency is inconsistent. We're evaluating open models and want to keep data in-house where possible.
[00:00:33] Tom: Also need tool-calling to hit internal APIs, and we have regulatory requirements for EMEA data residency.
[00:00:38] Maya: Understood. On the model side, are you leaning towards a particular family? Mistral, Llama variants, or newer open models?
[00:00:45] Rajiv: We're leaning open — want to avoid model provider lock-in. But biggest ask is long context: some of our specs are 40-60k tokens and in some cases 120k for archive searches.
[00:00:55] Ethan: Got it. So context length is a major driver. We recommend thinking in two buckets: interactive chat where 64k is typical and archive retrieval where you may need 128k or chunked retrieval plus smart KV cache.
[00:01:06] Lena: When you say KV cache, do you mean Redwood's prefix cache? We've seen references to KV cash in some notes, ha.
[00:01:11] Ethan: Ha, yeah KV cache — sometimes transcribed funny. It's prefix/KV cache to keep key-value states for decoder-only models, reduces re-computation for long contexts.
[00:01:19] Sofia: On deployment, we have a strong preference for Private (VPC) because of the data residency and our internal KMS, but we'd like to understand the cost delta vs Dedicated reserved capacity.
[00:01:28] Maya: Totally. Hosted gives fastest onboarding and lower ops; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Private lets you plug in your KMS and private control plane. Cost-wise, Private has higher setup and base cost but can be similar at scale. We'll share a cost matrix.
[00:01:39] Rajiv: For model selection, how do we reason about quality vs latency vs quantization? We have a hard 200ms token SLO for interactive flows, but for archive retrieval we can tolerate up to 1s/token.
[00:01:50] Ethan: Good callout. Quantization trades precision for performance. For interactive low-latency you can pick a smaller low-llm variant or quantized 8-bit profile; for higher quality offline retrieval you might run fp16 on dedicated GPUs. We can show benchmark numbers across model variants.
[00:02:03] [00:02:20] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[00:02:28] Maya: Another point — tool-calling. You mentioned internal APIs; do you need structured tool responses (like function calling) or just links/triggers?
[00:02:35] Tom: Ideally structured; we want the model to return JSON with fields to call downstream services. Also we want deterministic behavior for certain legal templates.
[00:02:43] Ethan: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output. For determinism you'll want guardrails: prompt templates, evals, and probably a reranking layer for high-stakes outputs.
[00:02:53] Lena: How about multilingual? We need English, German, French, Japanese and Korean at minimum. Some queries are code mixed.
[00:03:01] Ethan: Many open models have decent multilingual coverage but vary. We'll run multilingual evals across your representative prompts. Also consider smaller specialized models for languages with poor coverage, or ensemble routing by locale.
[00:03:12] Rajiv: Ensemble routing — can Redwood route to different model variants automatically?
[00:03:16] Maya: Yes. Smart routing can send requests by policy — latency, cost, region, or detected language. You can plug in a policy that routes German to a particular model.
[00:03:24] [00:03:42] Rajiv: There's also the question of hallucinations on QA. We're feeding specs and expect accurate quoting. How do you monitor/regressions?
[00:03:48] Ethan: Redwood Optimize ties evals to deploys. You can have prompt sets and unit tests; regressions trigger alerts and rollback policies. Also reranking and grounding to retrieved docs reduces hallucination.
[00:03:58] Sofia: From infra side, latency when using Private VPC — do you have data plane colocated model instances or is traffic routed via Redwood control plane?
[00:04:07] Ethan: Private offers a customer-managed data plane option: model serving can be colocated in your VPC; control plane remains separate unless you choose an on-prem package. That keeps traffic local and lets you use your KMS.
[00:04:15] Lena: Ok. What's the timeline for a pilot? We need to show a POC to ops and legal in three weeks.
[00:04:21] Maya: We can spin up a two-week pilot: 1) host a small dedicated pool for your workloads, 2) run benchmark suite (latency, throughput, multilingual quality), 3) deliver a short report. That fits three weeks if we start next week.
[00:04:32] Tom: Sounds good. For the benchmark, we want two workloads: interactive chat with 2k average context and retrieval-augmented with long context 64k-128k.
[00:04:41] Ethan: Perfect. We'll include Llama 3 variants, Mistral, and a couple of newer open models that are optimized for long context. We'll also show quantized and fp16 runs.
[00:04:48] [00:05:04] Lena: What about costs for the benchmark itself? If we need 128k context runs at scale, that sounds expensive.
[00:05:09] Maya: Benchmarks are typically cost-shared; Redwood can provide credits for pilot customers. We'll include estimated per-token costs in the benchmark plan and ways to optimize (caching, chunking).
[00:05:18] Rajiv: On stitching long docs — do you recommend using sliding windows or retrieval + condensation?
[00:05:23] Ethan: Retrieval + condensation is common: retrieve relevant chunks, summarize/condense into a compact context, then prompt. For true long-context models (128k+) you may skip condensation, but cost/latency tradeoffs apply. We'll demo both patterns.
[00:05:32] Tom: About compliance: SOC2 attestation, SSO via SAML, and audit logs — we need these for procurement.
[00:05:38] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and we have SOC2 docs. For Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. We'll attach the security pack.
[00:05:46] Sofia: Encryption at rest for model caches — is that supported?
[00:05:49] Ethan: Yes, caches and KV stores can be encrypted and integrated with your KMS. We'll surface exact options in the security doc.
[00:05:54] [00:06:10] Rajiv: Latency targets again — you mentioned batching and continuous batching; can we get both low-latency and throughput optimization?
[00:06:16] Ethan: You can tune batching windows and the runtime does continuous batching for small waits to improve throughput; for strict token SLOs you can pin to single-request execution paths and smaller instance types. It's a configuration trade-off.
[00:06:27] Lena: Any limitations on tool-calling? For example, calling internal DB that returns large JSONs.
[00:06:33] Ethan: Function outputs should ideally be compact. If the DB returns large payloads, use an ID reference and fetch server-side. But Redwood supports streaming responses so you can stream tool outputs progressively.
[00:06:42] [00:06:58] Tom: Regarding model updates and rollouts, we need canaries and automatic rollback if evals fail.
[00:07:04] Maya: Rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback to prior model variants. You can tie rollouts to eval metrics and traffic percentages.
[00:07:11] Rajiv: For embeddings and retrieval, do you offer native vector DB or integrations?
[00:07:16] Ethan: We integrate with popular vector DBs but also offer Redwood-cached embeddings and local vector store options in private deployments.
[00:07:24] Lena: One more — billing and metering, we need per-team cost breakdowns and token-level traces.
[00:07:29] Maya: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards and cost attribution. It's pretty granular for chargeback.
[00:07:36] [00:07:50] Rajiv: Are there known model tradeoffs for code-mixed inputs? Some models lose context when mixing Japanese and English.
[00:07:56] Ethan: True. We'll add code-mixed prompts to the benchmark and compare. We can also route specific locales to tuned models or use prompt-engineered prefacing.
[00:08:05] Lena: For the POC, do you recommend hosted or dedicated to start?
[00:08:09] Maya: Many customers start on Hosted to iterate quickly, then move to Dedicated or Private when they need throughput or residency. Given your compliance needs, starting with a Dedicated pool in your preferred region or a private pilot might be best. We can design both paths.
[00:08:20] Tom: Ok. Logistics — we'll need the security docs and a sample pilot contract for legal.
[00:08:25] Maya: We'll send both. Also a benchmark plan.
[00:08:30] [00:08:46] Sofia: Curious about on-prem option — if network cuts off, can the on-prem runtime continue serving?
[00:08:52] Ethan: The on-prem package can run a fully self-contained control plane if you need an air-gapped setup; otherwise the private data plane requires periodic control-plane heartbeats. We can detail failover modes.
[00:09:02] Rajiv: Great. Anything else we should flag?
[00:09:06] Maya: One small thing — for long-context accuracy, we'll suggest prompt templates and model ensembles plus a reranker. That tends to be the most cost-effective to reduce hallucinations.
[00:09:14] Tom: Makes sense.
[00:09:20] [00:09:36] (discussion continues with some cross talk and short clarifications about their infra)
[00:18:00] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood will send security pack and pricing matrix, SE will craft benchmark plan with multilingual and 64k/128k runs, customer to share compliance checklist and success criteria. Pilot target start next week.
[00:18:20] Lena: Yup, we'll prioritize internal stakeholders and send the checklist.
[00:18:25] Ethan: I'll include explicit model variants and the quantization profiles we'll test.
[00:18:30] Tom: Let's tentatively schedule bench kickoff for Tuesday.
[00:18:34] Maya: Works for us.
[00:18:40] [00:19:00] End of recording.
